question.text: Why do many Cat I/II AIFs prefer to pay Incentive Fee ONLY AT END OF FUND TENURE (or after major exits), rather than annually on NAV growth, per Chapter 6?

answer.text: SEBI prohibits annual incentive fee payments for Cat I/II funds
Annual incentive fees attract higher GST
To avoid 'double-counting' incentive on the same gain as NAV moves up-down-up, and to accommodate future loss-provisioning through clawback
Annual payment requires daily NAV computation, which Cat I/II cannot do

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6 conclusion to Example 6.3: annual incentive computation causes DOUBLE COMPUTATION of incentive on the same excess return (Y1 excess already earned carry; Y2 increase on top includes the Y1 base again). End-of-tenure payment solves this and also accommodates future NAV decline via clawback safety. The Trap: A is false (not prohibited); C mis-applies GST; D confuses reason (Cat I/II CAN do NAV, they don't want to do ANNUAL CRYSTALLISATION). Cross-Exam Context: Same mechanic in XIX-C. Cat III (XIX-E) pays HWM-crystallised carry periodically — different construction.
